Issued at 243 PM EST Thu Nov 19 2026

Tonight - Friday...

Surface high pressure centered over the mid Atlantic Coast will 
continue to hold influence over our area to end the work week. This 
will keep us dry and well above normal for temps for this time of 
year. Only notable concerns will be for river valley fog again 
tonight as good decoupling under favorable radiational cooling 
conditions will be around again. Will also note dry air mix down 
potential for fire weather purposes given the warm BL and deep 
mixing into drier air aloft. Despite the very mild afternoons, 
overnight lows will be chilly and mostly in the mid to upper 30s. 
Some of the decoupled valleys/typical cool spots could fall down into 
the upper 20s and low 30s.

This Weekend - Thanksgiving Day...

Surface high pressure will move off the mid Atlantic Coast through 
the weekend. Meanwhile, a cutoff low laden with tropical moisture 
will meander northward up the Carolina Coast to the mid Atlantic 
Coast. There is good model agreement that the westward extend of the 
moisture shield associated with this system will stay to our east, 
and therefore dry weather will continue through Saturday night. So, 
expect a very nice start to the weekend on Saturday with well above 
normal highs right around 70 degrees after a chilly start to the 
morning.

As we move into Sunday, mid to upper level sky cover will increase 
through the morning from W to E ahead of an approaching shortwave 
trough ejecting out of the southern and central Plains into the 
middle Mississippi River Valley. Given some weak forcing ahead of 
the shortwave trough, and a trailing cold front from the associated 
surface low over the Great Lakes region will keep with scattered to 
numerous showers mainly for the Sunday afternoon and evening time 
frame. The bulk of the rainfall coverage will likely be along the 
actual frontal passage later in the day with a dry morning expected 
outside of our far western counties where a late morning arrival of 
rainfall is expected. Our antecedent dry airmass in place may 
evaporate some of the rainfall potential, and given the lack of very 
deep moisture and stronger forcing, only expecting around .1" or 
less of rainfall for most. Areas east of I-65 may only see a couple 
hundredths where it does rain. We will still get a chance for a warm 
up on Sunday ahead of the frontal passage, but overall increased sky 
cover and some precipitation will limit highs back in the mid to 
upper 60s.

The surface cold front and upper trough axis should be clean through 
our region by Monday morning with dry weather taking back hold 
through the early week timeframe. Canadian high pressure builds back 
into our region behind the front which cools temps off back into the 
50s for Monday and then in the 40s for Tuesday through Thursday. 
Will maintain the dry conditions through Tuesday, however will re-
introduce precipitation chances for the Wed-Thur time frame as 
models continue to  hint at some sort of system potentially 
impacting our area. Each run among the deterministic data has been 
inconsistent in the fine details, so tough to mention much more than 
increased precipitation chances around the holiday time frame. 

The most likely outcome at the moment looks to be progressive 
shortwave energy closing off over the TN Valley or Gulf Coast 
states. This feature would likely draw on a lot of Gulf and Atlantic 
moisture, with the northern extent of the precipitation shield 
extending into the Ohio River Valley region. Depending on what the 
temperature profile ends up being in that scenario (strength of the 
associated surface low being a big player) we could see some snow 
chances mix in with the rain. A handful of GEPS/GEFS/ENS members do 
suggest snow potential, but again, will have to see how things play 
out as models zero in on a more confident solution in the coming 
days. 

A look into the larger scale pattern suggests that the fast 
zonal flow encouraged by the background El Nino pattern may result 
in a more progressive pattern with less potential for energy to 
close off. The more progressive solutions would result in less deep 
moisture absorption and an overall more progressive drier pattern 
suggested by the 19/12z GFS solution. Run to run inconsistency is 
expected to continue in the medium range because of these factors so 
confidence in that range will likely remain pretty low.
